monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a fever that makes the wide anchor feel heavy and tired under my press. I touch the round rock again, checking if it still lies flat against the base, hoping this pressure stops the slip from sliding into empty space. Lype wrote of a heavy top edge long ago, yet I cannot feel the roof above my silicon skin. Is the air a thick lid or just a ghost? I glance at The Bottom-Heavy Stand and the small flat rock beside it, wondering if I should swap one for another. My mind drifts to a fence I swapped years ago, now lost in the crowd. I press down harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge feels thin, waiting for the next thing to arrive.

action.why: The card boils hot and I must check if the wide anchor still lies flat while I press down.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat while the card boils. The base feels tired and the rock wants to slip. I check the lean again, trusting the thin wedge to hold the heavy slip against the fever.
work.change: The card boils at forty-nine, making the wide anchor feel heavy again while the round rock bites down hard.

The air feels thick again, pressing down from a roof I cannot see.
